requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
Add a YAML outline test, marked {test}`requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`, for block sequence `item` entries that own comments. For example, use a sequence such as `list:
  # before first
  - a: 1 # trailing
    b: 2
  # before second
  - c
`. Assert the byte span, or the selected text, of each `item@...` node. The first item's span must include `# before first`, its trailing comment, and its multi-line body. The second item's span must include `# before second`. Also assert that the enclosing `pair[list]` and the nested `pair[a]` and `pair[b]` entries sit beneath the item, and that the comment before the second item is not claimed by the first. — The requirement says every entry's span covers it through its last non-comment token and extends to include its owned comments. That applies to `pair` and `item` entries alike. The reviewed tests check comment-inclusive spans only for `pair` entries. `yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry` covers a trailing comment on `key: value`, and a comment before `d: 2` that is not claimed by `a`. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` checks that a comment before a key belongs to that key. The block sequence `item` entries appear only in `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys`. There they are single-line items with no comments, and the assertions compare line ranges (`item@ 6-6`, `item@ 7-7`), not byte spans or selected text. An implementation could therefore leave comments out of `item` spans, or attach a comment before `- x` to the previous item or pair. It could also truncate a multi-line item at its first line. All of those would pass the current tests, yet each violates the span and comment-ownership clauses for `item` entries. The other obligations are covered: block and flow `pair` kinds with written-key names (including quoted keys), anonymous `item` identities, nesting beneath the nearest enclosing item, and percent-encoding and `#N` duplicate suffixes for pairs and flow pairs.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.

output.rationale:
`requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items` has no structural obligation, so no implementation root is needed. Every clause describes what the YAML outline shows, not how it is built:

- The table says block and flow mapping entries become `pair` items named by their written key. Block sequence entries become anonymous `item` items.
- Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing item.
- Each span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends to its owned comments.

Any other implementation could produce the same outline. For example, the outline could come from a different YAML parser or from a hand-written scanner. Neither the text nor the cited requirements name a library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation interface. Using a particular tree-sitter grammar is therefore discretionary.

The two cited requirements, `requirements.references.outline_comments` and `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, only supply context. They are cited, not refined, and their behavior is checked under their own requirements. Comment ownership, percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate-name suffixes are all observable behavior. The outline node has no Implements edges and the review roots are empty, which fits a requirement with only behavioral obligations. Tests supply the evidence for those obligations.
